newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Johnston aims to boost margins.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Johnston aims to boost margins.

text.p: Local newspaper group Johnston Press Plc is aiming to drive up the margins of the titles it acquired last year from EMAP Plc, Johnston managing director Tim Bowdler said on Wednesday.
"The average margins we are making on the old EMAP titles is 16 percent which is well short of the 25 percent in the rest of our group," Bowdler said in a telephone interview.
"There is a substantial improvement we think we can make...The cost base has a long way to go in terms of coming down," he added.
Johnston paid 213 million stg last year to acquire 65 titles from EMAP, the largest expansion in the history of the Edinburgh-based publisher.
It has since sold one title in Cambridge but has held on to the remainder and Bowdler said that it had no plans to dispose of any more.
Acquisitions helped Johnston to boost turnover by 61 percent in 1996 to 165 million stg while pre-tax profit rose 43 percent to 24.1 million stg, towards the top end of analysts' forecasts.
Johnston shares had added 6p to 192.5p by 0945 GMT.
Johnston now has around 140 titles, with a roughly equal division between free and paid-for titles.
Bowdler said that the company would like to make further "bolt-on" acquisitions in a number of areas where the company already has a presence.
Its main areas of operations are Scotland, Yorkshire, much of eastern England and Sussex in the south.
The company's newsprint costs last year were 25 percent higher than in 1995 but Bowdler says they have now fallen back to the levels of two years ago.
He did not want to quantify how much Johnston would save on its annual print bill, stressing that some of the money would be reinvested in the titles in a bid to boost circulation.
